physicalNotes: Radius 0.08921418 Jupiter radii from Adams et al. 2021 (2021PSJ.....2..152A), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021PSJ.....2..152A/abstract): 6,378.1 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.00306 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Adams et al. 2021 (2021PSJ.....2..152A), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ADAMS_ET_AL__2021): P 2.255436 d
sources.shape: Adams et al. 2021 (2021PSJ.....2..152A), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ADAMS_ET_AL__2021): a/R* 17; Adams et al. 2021 (2021PSJ.....2..152A), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ADAMS_ET_AL__2021): inclination 89.9 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Adams et al. 2021 (2021PSJ.....2..152A), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ADAMS_ET_AL__2021): transit mid-time 2457010.0072 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 234 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
